subject: Large values for gradient of Latent Variable Model

messages.author: 6cf4f730b8d1254e
messages.subject: Large values for gradient of Latent Variable Model
parts:
Dear all,

I'm attempting to fit a latent variable model with TMB, that includes a second-order polynomial on the latent variable. However, on convergence the gradient is not zero.

Here's example code for a univariate case

#include <TMB.hpp>

template<class Type>
Type objective_function<Type>::operator() ()
{
  //declares all data and parameters used
  DATA_VECTOR(y);
  DATA_VECTOR(x);
 
  PARAMETER(b);
  PARAMETER(b1);
  PARAMETER(b2);
 
  //latent variables, u, are treated as parameters
  PARAMETER_VECTOR(u);
 
  int n = y.rows();
 
  vector<Type> eta(n);
 
  Type nll = 0.0; // initial value of log-likelihood
 
  for (int i=0; i<n; i++) {
  eta(i) = x(i)*b + u(i)*b1 + pow(u(i),2)*b2;
  }
 
  //latent variable is assumed to be from N(0,1)
 
    for (int i=0; i<n; i++) {
      nll -= dnorm(u(i),Type(0),Type(1),true);
    }
 
    for (int i=0; i<n; i++) {
      nll -= dpois(y(i), exp(eta(i)), true);
    }
  return nll;
}


And the R code to simulate some data and call TMB

library("TMB")
compile("lvm_poisson_quadratic_example.cpp")
dyn.load(dynlib("lvm_poisson_quadratic_example"))

#Simulate some univariate data
set.seed(07-03-2019)
b <- rnorm(1,1); u <- rnorm(20); b1 <- rnorm(1,1); b2 <- rnorm(1)

#True mean
eta <- b + u*b1 + u^2*b2
y <- round(exp(eta),0)

#Let TMB do its magic
model <- TMB::MakeADFun(
  data = list(y = y, x = rep(1,length(y))),
  parameters = list(b = b, b1 = b1, b2 = b2, u = u),
  random = c("u"), DLL = "lvm_poisson_quadratic_example")

#Estimate the parameters
fit <- optim(model$par, model$fn, model$gr,method="BFGS",control = list(trace=T,maxit=1000))

#check gradient
model$gr(fit$par)

This results to the values -54597583, 720315525 and 37266208 for the gradient. Any feedback or suggestions will be greatly appreciated!

messages.author: 258b98968d0ad8b9
messages.subject: Re: Large values for gradient of Latent Variable Model
parts:
The problem you experience occurs because it is possible to choose the outer parameters in a way such that the inner problem looks like a 4th order polynomial without the 2nd order term.
In this situation you are essentially integrating something like exp(-u^4) using the Laplace approximation. The result will be infinity, i.e. the outer optimization problem gets infinite reward by going into the bad parts of the parameter space where the Laplace approximation is inaccurate!
You'll see the negative log likelihood function has a ridge where it is most inaccurate (that's why you get the large gradients):

prof <- tmbprofile(model, 1, slice=TRUE, ytol=20)
plot(prof)


It is likely that in the future TMB will be able to handle your example using different integration techniques. For now the only easy option seems to be MCMC, e.g.:

library(tmbstan)
fit <- tmbstan(model)
plot(fit)

FWIW, another example with the same symptoms is given here: https://github.com/kaskr/laplace_accuracy

messages.author: 395bdca538bcae5d
messages.subject: Re: Large values for gradient of Latent Variable Model
parts: For those curious I ran MCMC on this. I think I'm having similar issues with my own model so I wanted to look deeper into this. Several parameters are bimodal in MCMC and it's easy to see why. Since b1 is so small a value of u=2 and u=-2 will lead to the same prediction. I've attached an output plot showing the behavior. So it seems it's not a LA-specific problem, but rather an ill-posed model more generally.

messages.subject: Re: Large values for gradient of Latent Variable Model
parts:
Although you're right about the example, the real (multivariate) model is run with sign constraints to prevent switching (and identifiability constraints)

With constraints, the model runs just fine in MCMC.
